title: Story of King Ibrahim and His Son (తెలుగు)
summary: Bakhtiyar related the story of King Ibrahim of Balkh: [TE]
keywords: story of king ibrahim and his son
full_text:
Bakhtiyar related the story of King Ibrahim of Balkh:

'King Ibrahim had an only son, Prince Ismail, whom he wished to train in the highest virtues of statecraft. When the prince reached eighteen years of age, the king sent him disguised as a common student to live in the provincial cities for two years.

Prince Ismail lived in student hostels, ate barley bread with poor weavers, helped farmers harvest wheat, and sat among the litigating peasants in the courts of justice.

He saw how corrupt magistrates favored the wealthy, how oppressive tax-collectors seized the milk-goats of widows, and how the honest poor suffered in silence.

When he returned to the palace, his father seated him upon the throne and asked: "What did you learn of your royal destiny, my son?"

Prince Ismail answered with tears in his eyes: "Father, I learned that a king is not a master to be served, but the chief servant of the realm! His palace exists to shelter the helpless, his army to defend the peaceful, and his treasury to feed the hungry. If a single orphan cries in the night from injustice, the king’s crown is stained with blood."

King Ibrahim embraced his son, weeping with joyful pride, and crowned him king before the assembled nation, and Prince Ismail governed for fifty years as the most beloved monarch of the East.'
moral: A prince’s true destiny is to serve his people with justice, empathy, and humble dedication. [TE]
